instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice and cook it the way you usually do.
Cut the peppers into 1/4-inch strips. Slice the onion thinly. Crush the garlic. Dice the tomatoes.
Heat 4 tbsp of the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onion and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the peppers and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and stir well. Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes. If it starts to stick, add a splash of water.
Add the tomatoes and half of the basil, torn. Raise the heat to medium and cook uncovered for 8 minutes, until the tomatoes turn saucy and the peppers are very tender but still hold their shape.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the balsamic vinegar, the last 1 tbsp oil and the rest of the basil, torn.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Great Italian Chefs (5.00, number of ratings not shown, so this is a fallback) leads: onion, garlic and basil softened in olive oil, peppers covered on low, tomatoes last, balsamic to finish. Savoring Italy and Giallo Zafferano agree on slow-cooked peppers and tomato added late; they differ on passata versus fresh tomato. The covered cooking is shortened from 30 minutes to 20 to fit 45 minutes. Served over rice to keep it gluten-free; it also keeps 3 days in the fridge.
